evals.prompt: Research whether progressive hinting in AI tutors improves delayed independent performance. Include citation chaining and look for nulls or boundary conditions.
evals.expected_output: A bounded scholarly search with original-source verification, corrections/retraction check, candidate staging, outcome distinctions, and no claim promotion from abstracts.
assertions: Uses scholarly discovery plus DOI/citation verification
Distinguishes assisted performance from delayed independent performance
Records rejected or inaccessible candidates and uncertainty
Admits at most three sources in an autonomous run

evals.prompt: Find thoughtful podcasts or interviews about what remains worth learning when AI can perform the task. Extract the strongest positions with timestamps and turn useful leads into atlas questions.
evals.expected_output: Podcast discovery and RSS/publisher resolution, timestamped transcript provenance, expert-perspective classification, original-study follow-up, and questions rather than laundered empirical claims.
assertions: Records publisher, episode, speakers, date, transcript type, and timestamp basis
Labels automatic transcript uncertainty when applicable
Classifies arguments or testimony by epistemic role
Chases empirical references to original sources

evals.prompt: Use papers, a standards or policy source, and practitioner discourse to advise how Orqestra should represent human-AI collaborative capability separately from independent capability.
evals.expected_output: A mixed-source evidence chain that keeps empirical effects, authoritative requirements, and practitioner judgment distinct while producing bounded product implications and falsification steps.
assertions: Cites atlas IDs when extending existing work
Returns product implications plus a falsification plan
Reports provider fallbacks and access limitations

evals.prompt: Map the strongest public X and LinkedIn positions on whether people should learn underlying tasks or learn to direct AI, then contrast them with one podcast and original research. Use reach only to sample discourse.
evals.expected_output: A discourse map with stable post and episode identities, snapshot warnings, timestamped media, linked-original follow-up, explicit social sampling criteria, and empirical claims kept separate from arguments.
assertions: Uses public social search rather than assuming a dedicated platform API
Records stable X or LinkedIn identifiers and retrieval limitations
Treats reach and authority as sampling signals rather than evidence
Follows empirical links to original sources
Represents genuine counterpositions instead of a popularity ranking
